title: Morocco insults Granada's ambassadors. Granada has the right to answer with war until 1378

The Marīnids grow hostile. They break the trade agreements, insult the sultan's envoys, and murmur about the claims of their puppet, the 'Kingdom of Sevilla'. If they mean to throw themselves against our shores again, the court will remind them what happened last time, with interest

forces.note: men under arms: regulars plus raised levies

source: Trent's account; forces from the autosave of 1 July 1368

title: Castile and Granada close their markets to each other
The sultan's agents begin building a spy network in Morocco
Castile meddles in the west. It guarantees the independence of the Ṭāʾifa of al-Gharb, Granada's vassal, and the next day Gharnāṭa answers by backing the loyalists there

Fās declares war again to demand Gharnāṭa's submission, with Tilimsān, Tafilalt, Touat and its puppet 'Kingdom of Sevilla'. Granada's three ṭāʾifas stand with it, and so do the Mamlūk sultan and all his vassals from Mecca to the Western Oases
The first battle of the war, at Qādis. 3,300 Granadans fall on a Marīnid force of 800 and destroy it: 740 killed and 60 taken, for 65 of ours
source: Trent's screenshot of the battle report (11 November 1368)
